newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar weakens after freight hike exemption.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar weakens after freight hike exemption.

text.p: Indian sugar markets weakened on Thursday after the commodity was exempted from increased rail freight rates in the government's railway budget, dealers said.
Sugar was firm on Wednesday following fears that the government may hike railway freight charges by 10/15 per cent.
"However the market turned weak today after the railway minister, in Wednesday's railway budget presentation, exempted sugar from the freight hike of 12 per cent," one broker said.
Dealers said sugar prices lost recent gains and fresh consumer buying eased.
Ready delivery sugar S-30 fell by 5/10 rupees to 1,240/1,275 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 eased by 2/5 rupees to 1,270/1,348 rupees per quintal.
